candidates.tagline: €28k rebrand ignored protests, copied a Belgian shelf company's logo
candidates.story: Galway City Council spent €28,000 overriding a 'Keep the Galway G' public campaign to unveil a new minimalist lowercase 'g' logo on September 17, 2026 — only to have it immediately identified as nearly identical to the logos of both Gondella, a Belgian shopfitting company, and Gousto, a British meal-kit firm.
candidates.why_funny: The council paused the rebrand due to public outcry, then quietly released it anyway — and within hours the €28,000 'g' was being compared side-by-side to a Belgian warehouse-shelving company's logo.
candidates.alt: Side-by-side comparison of Galway City Council's old elaborate circular G logo with coat of arms on the left versus its new plain maroon lowercase g design on the right — which critics note looks identical to a Belgian shopfitting firm's logo

candidates.tagline: Humanoid Robot Olympics 2026: things got sparky in the home straight
candidates.story: At the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing — a competition designed to prove that humanoid robots can sprint, jump, and kick like people — multiple robots collided, disintegrated, and caught fire mid-race, including one that burst into flames at the finish line of the 100-metre sprint on August 25.
candidates.why_funny: The entire premise of the games was that AI-powered humanoid robots can safely compete in athletics; several immediately proved that premise aggressively wrong by exploding on contact with the foam crash pad.
candidates.alt: Two humanoid robots in mid-air collision during a race at the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, one sparking and catching fire while robot limbs scatter across the blue athletics track
